correctness.rationale: The global maximum kills every other candidate except its unique nonneighbor. That partner is a peak exactly if second in the order; this gives each true matching edge mass 2/[n(n−1)] and each singleton the same matching-independent mass. A uniform prior therefore yields a uniform posterior over all completions on the uncovered vertices. Uniform random completion attains the Bayes upper bound on minimax success because relabeling makes its risk constant. Absence of r specified coupons has probability (1−rp_n)^m, proving the factorial moments and inclusion-exclusion. In the window, mp_n² vanishes and the factorial moments tend to λ^r, determining Poisson(λ); summing the reciprocal completion count uses u!(2u−1)!!=(2u)!/2^u. Above the window E[U]→0. Below it E[U]→∞ and the absent-edge indicators have nonpositive pairwise covariance, so U→∞ in probability. The n=2 and empty-sample boundaries work with (−1)!!=1 and an empty product equal to one, including the 0^0 term at q=1, m=0.
residual_risks: Only the promised labeled graph family with complete peak sets and fresh independent uniform orders is covered. The finite checker neither establishes optimality over estimators nor proves the asymptotic theorem; those follow analytically.

value.rationale: The matching-deleted family isolates a quantitative inference bottleneck in a natural censored graph experiment: the rare pair events alone carry information, but the structural promise can force completion without seeing all pairs. The exact achievable success and the non-coupon critical curve quantify this distinction at the optimal sampling scale, not merely identifiability or a sufficient bound.
residual_risks: No transfer to noisy peak sets, arbitrary hidden graphs, or unlabelled observations is claimed.
